**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — Section 10, Nonassignability (p0042)**

**What the document says.** The only assignment provision is a flat mutual consent requirement: "Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld." There is no change-of-control language anywhere in the Agreement, and Section 6 termination rights are limited to convenience-on-notice (when no SOW is outstanding) and uncured material breach.

**Why it fails.** The clause has no carve-out letting Clear Capital assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets. Even the playbook fallback requires a right to assign to successors on written notice, so this misses on a material term — our internal reorganizations and M&A would depend on RadialSpark's consent. The absence of a change-of-control termination or re-pricing right is favorable to us; the redline only confirms it rather than adding anything.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Appends a proviso to Section 10 that: (i) permits Company to assign without consent to an affiliate or an M&A successor on written notice; (ii) bars Contractor from assigning to a competitor of Company; and (iii) confirms a change of control of Company is not a deemed assignment and gives Contractor no termination, suspension or re-pricing right. The existing mutual "not unreasonably withheld" standard is preserved for all other assignments, keeping the edit minimal.
